{{Quote|If there's a spark of life, bacta will keep you going.|[[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]]|<ref name="Revenge">''[[X-Wing: Isard's Revenge]]''</ref>}}
'''Bacta''' was an organic chemical substance that consisted of gelatinous, translucent red [[Alazhi/Legends|alazhi]] and [[Kavam/Legends|kavam]] bacterial particles that were mixed within a colorless, viscous fluid known as [[Ambori/Legends|ambori]]. When a patient was exposed to bacta, the bacterial particles within sought out wounds and promoted rapid tissue regeneration while preventing the emergence of scar tissue. Bacta was often thought of as a "miracle fluid" and seemed to be effective against almost every type of injury and ailment across an incredible cross-section of [[Species/Legends|species]] throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. It was considered the best medicine available anywhere, replacing the previously used [[Kolto/Legends|kolto]].

==Description==
[[File:BactaTank-NEGWT.png|thumb|left|125px|A [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]]]]
{{Quote|Everyone uses Bacta. We've been using it so long, it's replaced most conventional medicine.|[[Uldir Lochett]]|<ref name="EotV">"[[Emissary of the Void]]"</ref>}}
Bacta could be administered via disposable [[Bacta patch/Legends|bacta patches]], direct injection, consumption (via [[bactade]]), a [[Salve/Legends|salve]], a [[Bio-Bacta]] tank, or submersion in a standard [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]]. For bacta immersion, the patient would be clothed in either just white shorts or a white sleeveless top and briefs depending on the person's gender. The method of administration depended on the severity of the wounds. It was imperative that bacta be applied in a solution of clear fluid which mimicked the body's own vital fluids.

Bacta tanks came in two varieties: large tanks for installation in medical facilities, and portable collapsible tanks for emergency use. Field tanks required patients to lie on their backs or stomachs while the bacta was run out and in again through filters.

Bacta had a cloying fragrance and a lingering sour taste that was reminiscent of flat or stale [[Lum/Legends|lum]].<ref name="X-Wing: Rogue Squadron">''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]''</ref> It reputedly stayed in the mouth and nasal cavity for weeks after immersion in a tank. The patch left a somewhat weaker-smelling residue.

==History==
{{Quote|You were feverish. I don't understand&hellip;your wound was bad but the medical droids should be able to ''do'' something. Not even bacta has been able to heal you.|[[Nomi Sunrider]] to [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]], after the latter sustained serious injuries during the [[Battle of Koros Major|siege of Empress Teta]]|<ref name="Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio)">[[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]]</ref>}}
[[File:Bacta_Grenade.jpg|right|thumb|A [[Bacta grenade/Legends|bacta grenade]]]]
Bacta was invented by the [[Vratix/Legends|Vratix]] on the planet [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]] in antiquity, with the galaxy at large learning of its properties around [[4100 BBY]].<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> The Vratix were willing to share the technology, but the substance could only be made in bulk on their homeworld, where the needed resources were abundant. Struggles on Thyferra were often caused by disputes over control of bacta, often between the two main producers of bacta, the [[Zaltin Corporation]] and the [[Xucphra Corporation]], or over the bacta the planet produced. Before its obsolescence, [[Kolto/Legends|kolto]] was used along with bacta for medical treatments. Bacta later outsold kolto and eventually replaced it altogether. After the reorganization of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the new [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] only allowed bacta to be produced on Thyferra, which was then stockpiled on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]].

More than [[0 ABY/Legends|six]] [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]],<ref name="RS I guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref> the Empire's [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Kohl Seerdon]] led an [[Attack on Thyferra|attack]] against [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] bacta supplies on Thyferra. [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] thwarted the attack, and Seerdon was killed.<ref name="RS I" />

Sometime before [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> the [[B-12 Bacta Transport]] ''[[Suveron]]'' was destroyed in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]], releasing half million tons of bacta in space. Although it was not suitable for medicinal use anymore, the bacta survived the vacuum of space and generated a large pocket of space gas known as the [[Linear Miasma]]. This unique phenomenon made the Linear Miasma popular among research communities.<ref name="SWG:TGTLM">{{SWGcite|exp=JtL|type=space|The Grand Tour - Linear Miasma|Endor system}}</ref>

At some point, [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] had the chemical sequence for bacta stored at his [[Mount Tantiss/Legends|stronghold]] on [[Wayland/Legends|Wayland]], possibly intending to develop a weapon to neutralize the properties of the compound. However, his scientists never developed a weapon, and the sequence remained stored on Wayland. When the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] gripped the galaxy, the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] conquered the planet Wayland where [[Shaper caste|Shapers]] managed to analyze the bacta formula whereupon they created a virus that targeted the alazhi plant on a genetic level. This was in order to create a bio-weapon designed to kill anyone who was treated by bacta. However, their plans were thwarted by [[Klin-Fa Gi]] along with [[Uldir Lochett]] as well as his crew.<ref name="EotV" />

During the [[Swarm War]], the [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]] staged a coup against the Thyferran government, which cut off the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance's]] supply of bacta during the [[Battle of Tenupe]], thus crippling the medical abilities of the Alliance.

==Potency==
[[File:Bacta_Potency.jpg|left|thumb|Rebel Alliance medics devised methods for getting more blends out of what bacta they could obtain.]]
{{Quote|So I was in for, what, a week?''"<br />"''Two days.''"<br />"''What? I should have been in there much longer than that for those injuries.|Corran Horn and a Zaltin medtech on Thyferra|<ref name="X:Bacta" />}}
Bacta was produced in various strengths and potencies based on many different factors. A batch's quality depended upon how the various ingredients were blended, the site where the ingredients were produced, and the Vratix [[Verachen]] that oversaw the blending. As Thyferra was the source of almost all the bacta in the galaxy while it was produced under the Imperial-backed duopoly of Xucphra and Zaltin, it was also the source of the strongest bacta. Such high-quality product was generally not exported; if it was, it was sold at incredibly high prices. Export-quality bacta was, typically, nowhere near as effective, meaning that more grievous injuries required longer exposure in order to be properly treated and healed.

==Allergies==
[[Ashern]] rebels once contaminated a portion of bacta. The contaminated bacta caused an allergy to bacta in all who used it. Upon discovery of the contamination, [[Ysanne Isard]] had much of it funneled into the black market. [[Ton Phanan]] and [[Gil Bastra]] both possessed an allergy to bacta. [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Tharil Tavira]] was also allergic, making his recovery from a stroke much more difficult.<ref name="IJ">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In terms of [[in-universe]] chronology, the earliest mention of bacta occurred in the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith|''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi - Dark Lords of the Sith'']] [[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|audio drama]]. It was also mentioned (later in galactic history) in [[Knights of the Old Republic 3|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 3]]. However, the author, [[John Jackson Miller]], admits that this may be a continuity error, and proposed a possible [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]], asserting that [[Marn Hierogryph]] was referring to some other thing coincidentally named bacta in the comic.<ref name="Faraway-''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic #3''">{{Faraway|url=comics/swknights/swkotor03.html|text=''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic #3''}}</ref> The issue was resolved with a reference in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' to bacta's discovery about a century before the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Tales of the Jedi'']] series.

Kolto tanks were the predecessor to bacta tanks, and were later replaced in favor of bacta, which explains the similarity in appearance between the two.
